text:
jamie_oncall: getting alerts for a cluster-wide spike of CUDA illegal memory access errors on two gpu nodes (gpu-45, gpu-46). errors started ~10:12 UTC, correlates with a batch rerun. oncall taking triage now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — #inc-4478900123 — Severity: high. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-illegal-access>.

maria_ml: saw this while running the embedding backfill. requests started returning 502 / runtime-exit for some customers. stack traces include misaligned reads after eviction.

dev_runtime: posting a shortened kernel log sample i pulled from gpu-45:

```
[  163.452117] GPU: CUDA: illegal memory access at 0x7f8b2d3f0 (pc 0x00007f8b2d3f)
[  163.452120] gpu_driver: misaligned pointer deref at 0x7ffd9c1e
[  163.452123] NVRM: XID 79: GPU page fault (PCI:0000:3e:00.0) 0x00000000012345
[  163.452128] trace: kernel: page_walk: invalid pte for addr 0x7f8b2d3f0 (unaligned offset)
```

jamie_oncall: that address pattern looks like a nullpage-ish drift + eviction race — not a simple OOM. could be kernel driver regression or SMMU pagewalk edge case.

eng_platform: taking node-level actions: cordoning gpu-45/gpu-46 now, will start draining pods with graceful timeout 60s. commands: `kubectl cordon gpu-45 && kubectl drain gpu-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60`

ops_coordinator: creating an external bridge for impacted customers and CS. tagging AcmeCorp and BeaconAnalytics as they reported elevated 5xx counts.

customer_success: AcmeCorp seeing ~3% of requests failing for their embedding pipeline since 10:15 UTC, they reported timeouts. escalated to enterprise response.

maria_ml: repro notes — I ran a tight loop of the embedding model with long seq_len and cold KV cache, reproduced illegal access in ~15-20 minutes on a local dev node with the same runtime build. attaching snippet of the request pattern: `batch_size=1, seq_len=4096, kv_cache_enabled=true, model=llama-2-13b-q4`

dev_runtime: quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily disable KV cache for long-seq requests, 2) route long seq embeddings to CPU pool, 3) roll back the last driver/kernel patch on affected nodes. i can flip a runtime flag to force soft fallback.

jamie_oncall: do the runtime flag now — we need immediate customer relief. dev_runtime, share command for config change.

dev_runtime: run on affected nodes / runtime config: 

```
# set env to disable persistent kv caching
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/runtime-gpu REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=false
# enable CPU fallback for model routing
kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/router REDWOOD_FORCE_CPU_FALLBACK=true
# restart runtime svc pods on node
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart daemonset/runtime-gpu
```

deploy_bot: ROLLBACK TRIGGERED: runtime-service v2.3.4 -> v2.3.2 via emergency rollback. Triggered by jamie_oncall.

eng_platform: rolled out cordon + drain for gpu-45, beginning restart of worker services on replacement node (gpu-72) to take traffic. draining gpu-46 now.

maria_ml: after turning off KV cache on the daemonset I see a drop in illegal access logs on gpu-45 within 90s. requests still slower but error rate down to baseline.

ops_coordinator: customer bridge up; CS joined. AcmeCorp on the bridge, logged incident -> CS will update status page.

customer_success: posting status note: "We are investigating elevated errors on embedding requests; temporary routing changes applied to reduce impact, ETA for full resolution unknown."

jamie_oncall: next steps: 1) confirm repro steps and collect full dmesg+perf trace, 2) if repro deterministic, prepare kernel-driver bisection, 3) keep rollback in place and prioritize a hotfix release. also consider automatic fallback policy for long-seq jobs to prefer CPU by default if KV cache warmup likely to cause eviction.

dev_runtime: uploading a short perf trace and repro script to the incident folder: `s3://redwood-incidents/4478900123/repro.tar.gz`. it includes a small harness that repeatedly runs the seq_len=4096 workload and captures `dmesg` on crash.

maria_ml: quick findings from the perf trace: fault happens during pagewalk when page is re-mapped concurrently by eviction. we see a race between the page table update and the GPU pagewalker — kernel pte points to a partially updated mapping (unaligned offset).

eng_platform: we've kept two spare nodes ready to accept traffic. migrating AcmeCorp traffic to gpu-72 and gpu-73. routing changes applied via router rollout at 10:37 UTC.

jamie_oncall: are there customer-side mitigations we can suggest?

customer_success: recommend reducing batch sizes and seq lengths for now; apply retries with jitter. also suggest toggling to the hosted embeddings CPU endpoint where latency is acceptable.

ops_coordinator: tagging security and compliance since AcmeCorp is in regulated space. notifying legal and account execs.

dev_runtime: for a potential hotfix, we should add a safety check in the pagewalk handler to validate PTE canonicalization and alignment before issuing DMA to the device. patch candidate available at branch `hotfix/unaligned-check-447890`.

jamie_oncall: good. assign owners: dev_runtime -> produce PR + test; eng_platform -> validate node kernel/drivers and prepare canary; maria_ml -> provide reproducible harness steps and golden logs; ops_coordinator -> coordinate customer updates.

incident-bot: Reminder — please add postmortem checklist items to the incident doc: RCA, timeline, mitigation, customer impact, and follow-ups.

maria_ml: adding a note: observed error signature differs slightly from previous illegal-access incidents — mismatch is the unaligned offset in kernel trace, not an obvious OOM or pointer corruption in userland. looks like a pagewalk corner-case.

jamie_oncall: closing loop for initial mitigation: rollback applied, KV cache disabled, traffic drained off affected nodes, customer bridge open. monitoring for 30m. if errors stay low we'll keep this as mitigated and proceed with bisection + hotfix path. :thumbsup:

customer_success: AcmeCorp acknowledged mitigation, continuing to monitor.

eng_platform: last note — keep logs for 90 days in case we need cross-team deeper analysis.

jamie_oncall: end of live thread update — will post final incident summary when RCA is ready.
